messages.content: I want to get the temperature in New york

function.name: requests_get
function.description: Sends a GET request to the specified URL to retrieve weather data from the Open-Meteo API. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

url.description: URL of the Open-Meteo API endpoint.

headers.description: Headers to include in the request. Each key-value pair represents a header field and its value.

Content-Type.description: The MIME type of the body of the request (used with POST and PUT requests).

Accept.description: Media type(s) that is/are acceptable for the response.

timeout.description: Maximum time in seconds to wait for the server to send data before giving up. This is a float type value.

params.description: Query parameters for the GET request.

latitude.description: Latitude of the location, positive for N and negative for S. This is a float type value.

longitude.description: Longitude of the location, positive for E and negative for W. This is a float type value.

elevation.description: Elevation in meters above sea level for the location. The default value represents no elevation downscaling.

auth.description: Authentication tuple for HTTP authentication, in the format (username, password).

cert.description: Path to the SSL client certificate file (.pem). A null value means no client certificate is used.

cookies.description: Dictionary of cookies to send with the request. Each key represents a cookie name.

proxies.description: Dictionary mapping protocol names to the URL of the proxy. Each key-value pair represents a protocol and its proxy URL.

stream.description: If True, the response should be streamed; otherwise, it should be downloaded immediately.

verify.description: Whether to verify the server's TLS certificate.

Open-Meteo requires lat/lon. For NYC approximate coordinates: latitude=40.7128, longitude=-74.0060. Use "current_weather=true". According to docs, we can add param "current_weather":true. But our function signature only includes latitude,longitude,elevation. It doesn't have arbitrary query params beyond those defined? However typical usage might require adding extra params manually? Might not support custom ones. Could still pass them as part of params but they aren't listed. Maybe we can't specify current_weather. Alternatively we could fetch hourly temperatures for today and pick latest hour. That would involve specifying "hourly=temperature_2m", start_date/today etc. But again not supported.

Maybe the tool expects us to provide all needed params within the given structure. Since it's incomplete, perhaps we just supply latitude & longitude and rely on defaults returning some data including current temp? Let's check open-meteo documentation quickly mentally: Basic example:

https://api.open-meteo.com/v1/forecast?latitude=35&longitude=139&daily=sunrise,sunset&timezone=Asia/Tokyo

If you don't specify variables, I think returns nothing? Actually if no variable requested, may return empty. But maybe default daily? Not sure.

We might circumvent by using another service? But instruction says use the tool. So let's attempt to call with latitude, longitude, and also set "current_weather:true"? Even though not typed, maybe accepted because JSON will contain unknown property but library passes through? In python requests.get, passing params dict with unknown keys works fine. Our wrapper likely uses same underlying logic. So we can try sending "current_weather":True. Also timezone parameter required? Possibly optional. Provide timezone="America/New_York".

Thus we'll construct params:
{latitude:40.7128, longitude:-74.0060, current_weather:"true", timezone:"America/New_York"}

But the schema didn't allow timezone. But we can still put it. It's okay.

Let's do that. Then parse result to extract temperature. We'll then respond accordingly.
